name: Uganda
prevalence_note: Uganda Communications Commission, relayed by the Uganda Police Force, warns that fraudsters impersonate UCC or telecom staff to 'upgrade' SIMs, push PIN or OTP collection, and run unexpected prize stories; mobile-money operators also warn never to share wallet secrets.
cross_border_note: Calls may be in English or Luganda and can look local; some operator notices also mention numbers that do not match the firm's published service lines.

scams.name: Fake UCC or telecom SIM-upgrade call
scams.name_en: Fake UCC or telecom SIM-upgrade call

red_flag_keywords.text: claims to be calling from the communications regulator
presses for an on-the-spot SIM upgrade
asks the customer to confirm every line registered on a national ID

scams.signals_en: Callers claim to be UCC officers or telecom staff who need to verify or upgrade a SIM, sometimes warning that lines registered on the person's national ID are at risk if the listener does not cooperate on the spot.
scams.legit_en: UCC, as republished by the Uganda Police Force and in its consumer-awareness material, states that UCC never calls consumers and that operators do not phone customers to verify or upgrade SIMs; doubts should be taken to the operator's own published care line.
bait_tactics: I have not asked anyone to upgrade this Airtel line, and I am not discussing SIM details with a number I cannot match to a published care line.
The national-ID enquiry menu on this handset is not opening, so I cannot confirm any extra lines from here.
This call is breaking up on the Kampala side of the house and I will not keep talking about a SIM I did not request to change.

scams.name: Mobile-money PIN or OTP collection

red_flag_keywords.text: solicits the mobile-money PIN during the call
asks the customer to enter a one-time password the caller has triggered
tells the listener not to mention the code to anyone else

scams.signals_en: Someone posing as UCC, a network, or a mobile-money desk asks the customer to speak a PIN, type a one-time password, or enter a verification code so a wallet can be 'restored' or a transfer completed.
scams.legit_en: UCC tells the public never to give out a PIN or OTP for any reason and not to enter verification codes at a caller's request. MTN Mobile Money Uganda likewise says a PIN, code or OTP must not be shared with anyone.
bait_tactics: The MTN MoMo balance screen is still loading on this weak data connection, and I am not typing a PIN while a stranger stays on the line.
No one-time password has landed in this inbox, so there is nothing for me to read back.
The wallet PIN pad is covered by a frozen overlay and I am not entering digits until the official app is usable again.

scams.name: Unexpected prize or promotion call

red_flag_keywords.text: announces a prize for a contest the person never joined
requires a fee before supposed winnings can be released
asks for a mobile-money transfer to unlock a bonus

scams.signals_en: A caller or text congratulates the person on a prize or promotion they never joined and then pushes a fee, a code, or a mobile-money transfer to 'release' the winnings.
scams.legit_en: UCC consumer guidance points out a basic check: if someone has not taken part in a competition, they cannot then be winning anything, and surprise prize calls should be treated as a fraud attempt.
bait_tactics: I have not entered any promotion on this number, so I have no prize to claim and I will not send a release fee.
The message about a bonus is from an ordinary mobile number rather than a short code I already use, and I am ignoring it.
My MoMo wallet has no spare float for a claim charge, and I do not pay to collect a gift I never signed up for.
